Senses.Explanation: To hug a bridge pillar while washing is to cling to the fixed support while trying to perform an action around it. Chan records preserve the fuller forms washing while embracing a bridge pillar and washing the feet while embracing a bridge pillar. They pair the image with launching a boat while holding its cable, feeling along a wall, or remaining unable to move freely; Baizhang Yu contrasts it with his own response. The record uses the bodily awkwardness as a comparison for being impeded by the very thing one holds.
